pending.title: Hexanol, which does not block gap junctions, does not alter head shape
pending.hypothesis: Octanol engages a planarian gap-junction channel better than hexanol does, consistent with the paper's premise that hexanol 'does not efficiently block gap junction channels'.

pending.title: Free energy is minimized only when every cell occupies a unique inferred place
pending.hypothesis: In the paper's eight-cell active-inference model, free-energy descent run to a steady state reaches the target form (every cell at its own distinct target location with the correct identity) from every initial condition tried, and no non-target stationary state has free energy at or below that of the target form.

pending.title: HCN2 modelled as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small Vmem gradients
pending.hypothesis: In a coupled-cell bioelectric model of the anterior stage-15 Xenopus neurula built with the paper's stated ingredients (Table 1 concentrations, 0.1x MMR medium, three regions whose K+/Cl- leak differences give a hyperpolarized neural tube near -50 mV and lateral neural folds/ectoderm near -5 mV, Kir channels, voltage-sensitive gap junctions) and BETSE's HCN2 kinetic model (V1/2 = -99 mV shifted +20 mV by cAMP, Na+:K+ permeability 0.2), adding homogeneously expressed HCN2 opens it preferentially in the hyperpolarized tube, drives tube cells further negative, and leaves the depolarized lateral regions essentially unchanged, i.e. it amplifies the existing Vmem gradient rather than shifting all regions uniformly.

pending.title: Native HCN2 activity is not required for normal brain patterning
pending.hypothesis: The GYG->AAA mouse HCN2 construct used in the paper can still co-assemble with wild-type HCN2 subunits (the premise that makes it dominant-negative), so that a construct which fails to disrupt patterning can be read as evidence that native HCN2 activity is not required.

pending.title: Animal senses use the same ion channel mechanisms found in bacteria
pending.hypothesis: For each of the four senses named (touch, taste, temperature, hearing), at least one ion channel that transduces that sense in animals has a predicted structure containing the fold of a known bacterial ion channel, as measured by TM-score, clearly above the score a non-channel membrane protein reaches against the same bacterial channel.

pending.title: Selection for locomotion under random actuation evolved derandomizing shapes
pending.hypothesis: In a voxel soft-body simulation where each contractile voxel's phase offset is random and fixed per clade (so selection can only change which voxels exist and which are contractile), selection for net displacement yields designs that move much farther than random designs under the same random actuation, and the gain depends on the evolved arrangement of passive and contractile voxels rather than on the particular phases.

pending.title: Adding hydrodynamics and random actuation made simulated gaits match living ones
pending.hypothesis: Designs evolved for locomotion on simulated land with evolvable (finely tuned) actuation phases spend a large fraction of their evaluation airborne, whereas designs evolved with first-order hydrodynamics (reduced gravity plus surface drag) and random clade-fixed phase offsets stay in contact with the ground almost all the time, as living deciliated organisms do (93.3% vs 52.7% ground contact in the paper).

pending.title: Bilayer curvature from differential swelling (Timoshenko)
pending.hypothesis: If the Timoshenko bilayer law holds for a fabricated hydrogel bilayer, the change in curvature of a 3 mm wide, 30 mm long printed strip between the reference state (30 % relative humidity, 23 C) and equilibrium in water, predicted from independently measured layer thicknesses h1 and h2, moduli E1 and E2 and free swelling strains eps1 and eps2 of single-layer strips as kappa = 6(1+m)^2 / (h [3(1+m)^2 + (1+mn)(m^2 + 1/(mn))]) (eps1 - eps2) with m = h1/h2 and n = E1/E2, equals the measured change in curvature of the same bilayers; and the time to reach 1 - 1/e of the final curvature change scales as the square of the total thickness.

pending.title: Bilayer curvature from differential swelling (Timoshenko)
pending.hypothesis: If a pine cone scale behaves as a Timoshenko bilayer, the change in curvature between the dry and wet state predicted from the measured active-layer thickness h1, passive-layer thickness h2, modulus ratio n = E1/E2 and swelling-strain mismatch delta_eps, kappa_pred = 6(1+m)^2 / (h [3(1+m)^2 + (1+mn)(m^2 + 1/(mn))]) * delta_eps with m = h1/h2 and h = h1 + h2, equals the measured curvature change (or, for a scale of free length L, the measured opening-angle change theta = L * kappa) of the same scales to within the measurement uncertainty.
